note: Rows published automatically by the weekend pipeline before editor review. Same columns as the sheet plus Auto=1. Rows move to the sheet once reviewed; the sheet wins on ID clashes.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: they're aiming to raise, wait for it, $100 billion. In other words, like three months of compute, and that would make it the largest IPO ever.
rows.Claim: Anthropic is aiming to raise about $100bn in its IPO, which would be the largest IPO ever, ahead of SpaceX's June 2026 listing.
rows.Evidence: Anthropic filed its S-1 publicly on 26 Oct 2026. Reports on the offering put the fundraising target at up to $100bn at a $1.5-2tn valuation; the final size is not yet set. SpaceX raised about $85-86bn in its June 2026 IPO, the current record, so a $100bn raise would be the largest ever.
rows.Notes: Offering size is a reported target, not a filed term; the specific 16 Nov date he mentions was not confirmed in the sources found (reports say 'by the end of November').

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: $16.3 billion in the first half of 2026 That is 14x year over year.
rows.Claim: Anthropic's S-1 shows $16.3bn of revenue in H1 2026, 14 times H1 2025.
rows.Evidence: The S-1 reports revenue of $16,286m for the six months to 30 Jun 2026 versus $1,163m a year earlier, a 14.0x increase. Quarterly figures in analyses of the filing put Q1 2026 at $4.7bn and Q2 at $11.6bn, matching his Q2 figure.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Seven founders, yes, they have seven, are going to hold 50.1% of the voting power through a single class F share.
rows.Claim: Anthropic's seven co-founders will control 50.1% of the voting power through a single Class F share.
rows.Evidence: The S-1 describes one share of Class F stock, issued to a Founder LLC before the offering, carrying 50.1% of total voting power on matters submitted to stockholders generally. The filing names seven co-founders (Dario and Daniela Amodei, Tom Brown, Jack Clark, Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish, Chris Olah).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: That narrative basically just got completely refuted because it turns out that $80 billion loss is a phantom number.
rows.Claim: Anthropic's reported ~$80bn H1 2026 loss is mostly a non-cash accounting charge from revaluing convertible notes, not an operating loss.
rows.Evidence: The S-1 shows an H1 2026 net loss of $80.7bn, of which $72.4bn is the change in fair value of convertible notes, derivative liabilities and SAFEs, which the filing attributes mainly to the rise in Anthropic's valuation. The operating loss for the half was only $0.7bn (and Q2 showed a GAAP operating profit of about $1.0bn). The charge is non-cash, as he says.
rows.Notes: About $8.8bn of 'other expense' is not explained by the revaluation, so 'phantom' fits roughly 90% of the loss rather than all of it. Anthropic row: extra scrutiny per Methodology s.9; Sacks is a public critic of Anthropic's policy positions.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: They've raised something like, I think it was around $110 billion roughly, and they've only spent about $9 or $10 billion throughout the entire course of this business.
rows.Claim: Anthropic has raised about $110bn and has only consumed about $9-10bn of it.
rows.Evidence: The S-1 says Anthropic had raised $141.1bn in aggregate by 30 Jun 2026 and held $112.4bn of cash and equivalents plus $19.3bn of short-term investments ($131.7bn). The gap, about $9.4bn, matches his $9-10bn of cash consumed. His raised figure is low by about $30bn, which does not change the point (very little of the capital has been spent).
rows.Notes: Same point as Chamath's 'total net burn ... like $9 billion or $10 billion' (26:22). Jason's '$112 billion in cash' (3:20) also matches the filing.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: I think their gross margin is now something like 85 percent.
rows.Claim: Anthropic's gross margin is now about 85%.
rows.Evidence: Analysis of the S-1 puts H1 2026 cost of revenue at about $2.4bn on $16.3bn of revenue, an implied gross margin of about 85%, up from about 12% in H1 2025 and about 40% for FY2025.
rows.Notes: The S-1 itself does not print a gross-margin line; total compute and infrastructure expense (including training) was $8.9bn in H1 2026, so the 85% excludes training compute. Friedberg's '85% incremental gross margin' (12:53) rests on the same figures.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: Either to ban it outright, as Bernie Sanders and Elizabeth Warren and AOC want to do. They basically want 20-year jail sentences for developers of super intelligence, and they want corporate death penalty for companies that build super intelligence.
rows.Claim: The Democratic agenda on superintelligence is to ban it, with 20-year prison terms and a 'corporate death penalty', as Sanders, Warren and AOC want.
rows.Evidence: The Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act, introduced in Sep 2026 by Sen. Bernie Sanders and Rep. Greg Casar, does ban superintelligence, with up to 20 years in prison for individuals and a 'corporate death penalty' for companies, and creates a federal AI agency. AOC is a House cosponsor. But Elizabeth Warren does not appear among the sponsors or cosponsors found, and the House bill has about a dozen cosponsors out of some 213 House Democrats. Reporting describes it as a 'prohibitionist left flank', with other Democrats (e.g. Sen. Mark Kelly) pursuing different approaches. Presenting it as 'the Democrat agenda' overstates it.
rows.Notes: The bill's provisions are described accurately; the rating is for naming Warren and for presenting a minority bill as the party's agenda (Methodology rule 4).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: I think the latest numbers from like Fed GDP now, I think it was 3.7% in Q3 and it was 2.5% in the first half of the year.
rows.Claim: The Atlanta Fed's GDPNow had Q3 2026 growth at 3.7%, after about 2.5% in the first half.
rows.Evidence: GDPNow estimated Q3 2026 real GDP growth at 3.7% (annual rate) on 1 and 6 Oct 2026, easing to 3.6% on 8 Oct. BEA's Sep 2026 release puts Q1 2026 growth at 2.5% and Q2 at 2.2%, so the first half averaged about 2.35%, close to his 2.5%.
rows.Notes: His follow-on inference that 'all of the economic growth' comes from the AI build-out is an interpretation and is not rated. Later (1:16:24) he says growth 'was 2.5% in the last quarter'; Q2 was 2.2%.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: that can be seen very clearly in him having the worst approval rating of his entire career
rows.Claim: Trump's approval rating is at the lowest point of his career.
rows.Evidence: Several pollsters recorded career lows for Trump in 2026: The Economist/YouGov had him at 33% approve / 62% disapprove in Aug 2026, its lowest for either term and below his previous low of 34% a few weeks earlier.
rows.Notes: Verified for The Economist/YouGov series; we did not check every pollster or the averages.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: What this shows you is that Microsoft's revenue went from 198 billion to 332 billion in the last four years, while staff only increased by 2000 people.
rows.Claim: Microsoft's revenue rose from $198bn to $332bn in four years while headcount rose by only about 2,000.
rows.Evidence: Microsoft's FY2022 10-K reports revenue of $198.3bn and about 221,000 full-time employees; its FY2026 10-K reports about 223,000 full-time employees, and FY2026 revenue was $331.8bn. So revenue rose about 67% while headcount rose about 2,000.
rows.Notes: Headcount was not flat in between: it rose to about 228,000 in FY2025 and fell 5,000 in FY2026. Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees in Oct 2026, as he says. His conclusion that AI does not cause job loss is an opinion and not rated.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: There's about 1650 that spend between 1 and 10 million, and only 250 customers spend 10 million and more.
rows.Claim: About 1,650 Anthropic customers spend $1-10m a year and only about 250 spend $10m or more.
rows.Evidence: The S-1 says that, as of 30 Sep 2026 (trailing-twelve-month revenue), Anthropic had more than 11,900 customers above $100k, more than 1,900 above $1m and about 250 above $10m. That leaves about 1,650 in the $1-10m band and about 10,000 in the $100k-1m band, as he says.
rows.Notes: His 'about 40 million individuals and small businesses spending under 100K' is not in the filing excerpts reviewed and is not rated.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: And I think in order to do that, the price is probably now going to come in between 1.3 on the low end to 1.7 on the high end.
rows.Claim: Anthropic's IPO will price at a valuation of about $1.3-1.7tn, around $1.5tn.
rows.Evidence: Reported talk for the offering is a $1.5-2tn valuation; no price range had been filed at recording time.
rows.Notes: Rule (auto): Accurate if Anthropic's IPO prices at an implied market capitalization (offer price x shares outstanding after the offering, as reported in the final prospectus or by Reuters/Bloomberg) of $1.3tn to $1.7tn; False if below $1.3tn or above $1.7tn. Void if no IPO prices by 30 Jun 2027. Conflicts with his earlier call AIA-20260926-14 ('around $1tn or less'); each is scored on its own rule (Methodology rule 8). He revised his view on air because the S-1 showed more cash than he had assumed.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: Meta's net cash is negative two. It is 80 billion of cash and short turns and 82 billion of debt.
rows.Claim: Meta's cash and short-term investments roughly equal its debt, leaving net cash of about zero.
rows.Evidence: Meta's 10-Q for the quarter to 30 Sep 2026 shows $11.2bn of cash and equivalents plus $71.2bn of marketable securities ($82.4bn), against $80.9bn of long-term debt and no short-term debt line. Net cash is about +$1.5bn, so his figures are swapped (cash about $82bn, debt about $81bn), but the point stands: Meta's net cash is roughly zero after its capex spending.
rows.Notes: Responds to Chamath's 'Meta had negative 1.2 billion of cash' (26:22), which the same 10-Q also shows to be about zero rather than negative. Sign error noted, not penalised (Methodology rule 3).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: the amount of money that they need to raise through the end of 27th, it's 30% of all of what treasury is about to issue in that same period.
rows.Claim: The AI companies' borrowing needs through end-2027 equal about 30% of all Treasury issuance over the same period.
rows.Evidence: We could not find the source of the 30% figure. Published estimates put global AI-related debt issuance above $500bn in 2026 (Morgan Stanley) and hyperscaler issuance above $1tn through 2027 (Citrini Research), and JPMorgan has warned the issuance adds pressure on Treasury yields. Whether this is 30% of Treasury issuance depends on whether gross or net Treasury issuance is meant; against net issuance the order of magnitude is plausible, against gross issuance (tens of trillions a year) it is far lower.
rows.Notes: The figure comes from a chart his research team prepared; it was not shown with a source.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: Which is public information, and those PACs have supported candidates.
rows.Claim: Anthropic has given large sums to political action committees that back candidates, and this is public.
rows.Evidence: Anthropic gave $20m in Feb 2026 to Public First Action, a super PAC backing candidates who favour AI regulation (it has run ads for Republican Sens. Marsha Blackburn and Pete Ricketts), and later reportedly raised its support to $40m. In Apr 2026 it also registered a corporate PAC, AnthroPAC, with the FEC.
rows.Notes: The quote completes his line at 41:49 ('they have given huge amounts of money to PACs'). His claim that Anthropic is hiring many former Biden and Trump officials was not verified and is not rated. Anthropic row: extra scrutiny; Sacks, the former White House AI adviser, has accused Anthropic of seeking regulatory capture.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: If you go back to August, Anthropic published a very interesting blog talking about how they were using RSI, and 26 percent, they had a chart showing that 26 percent of their tasks that were involved in basically trying to create the next generation of models, they were already were using RSI to do that.
rows.Claim: Anthropic published a blog saying it already uses recursive self-improvement for 26% of the work of building its next models.
rows.Evidence: Anthropic's essay 'When AI builds itself' (updated 18 Sep 2026) reports rapidly growing use of Claude in its own AI research and development; secondary reports cite a figure of about 26% of its AI R&D now led by Claude, up from near zero early in 2026. But the essay defines recursive self-improvement as an AI 'capable of fully autonomously designing and developing its own successor' and says Anthropic is not there yet. Saying Anthropic is 'already using RSI' reverses what the publication says.
rows.Notes: The 26% figure itself is supported only by secondary reports; we could not match it to a specific chart. Anthropic row: extra scrutiny (Methodology s.9); editor to confirm.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: They're at about 100 billion in revenue this year, which is like a third of a Google, a quarter of an Apple.
rows.Claim: Anthropic will have about $100bn of revenue this year.
rows.Evidence: About $100bn is Anthropic's expected annualized run-rate at the end of 2026 (reports say it expects $110bn+), not its revenue for the year. The S-1 shows $16.3bn of revenue in H1 2026; Q3 was about $16.9bn; estimates of 2026 revenue are around $60bn. Comparing a year-end run-rate with Google's and Apple's annual revenue overstates Anthropic's size about twofold.
rows.Notes: Earlier (3:20) he correctly noted that the $100bn figure is a run-rate projection.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: The people using it frequently versus daily, we're still talking about 10 and 20 percent here.
rows.Claim: Gallup finds only about 10% of US workers use AI daily and about 20% frequently.
rows.Evidence: Gallup's survey of 22,000+ US workers (fall 2025, published Jan 2026) found 12% use AI daily at work and about a quarter use it frequently (several times a week or more); nearly half use it at least a few times a year.
rows.Notes: Slightly understated (12% and about 25%); the point that daily use is still low stands.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Q3 earnings wiped out about 500 billion in market cap. Why? For two straight quarters, Google missed on search revenue, even though searches are growing massively.
rows.Claim: Alphabet lost about $500bn of market value after Q3 earnings, having missed on search revenue for two straight quarters.
rows.Evidence: Alphabet's Class A shares fell 12.6% on 29 Oct 2026, to $283.82, a loss of roughly $500bn of market value. Search & other revenue was $63.35bn, up 12% (after 17% in Q2), and missed analyst estimates for the second straight quarter. Google Cloud revenue doubled to $30.7bn and free cash flow was negative (-$9.1bn), as he also says.
rows.Notes: Same figures as Sacks's row on search revenue (1:11:34).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: Last year, the Google Cloud business for this quarter was generating 3.5 billion of operating income. This quarter, it's over 11 billion of operating income
rows.Claim: Google Cloud's quarterly operating income rose from about $3.5bn a year ago to over $11bn.
rows.Evidence: Google Cloud's operating income was $11.1bn in Q3 2026 versus $3.6bn in Q3 2025, on revenue of $30.7bn (up 103%). Google Services operating income rose about 17% to $39.2bn, matching his '33.5 to 39'.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: I think we saw this battle play out recently where Jeff Dean and others left Google
rows.Claim: Jeff Dean and other senior AI researchers recently left Google.
rows.Evidence: Jeff Dean announced in Aug 2026 that he was leaving Google after 27 years to start a company, Discovery Loop; reports named Sanjay Ghemawat and Quoc Le among colleagues leaving with him.
rows.Notes: His theory of why they left (compute going to cloud customers) he flags as unconfirmed; it is not rated.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: It increased from $56 billion to $63 billion.
rows.Claim: Google search revenue still grew year over year, from $56bn to $63bn, even as its share of Alphabet's revenue fell below 50%.
rows.Evidence: Search & other revenue was $63.35bn in Q3 2026 versus $56.57bn a year earlier, up 12%. It was 49.7% of Alphabet's $127.6bn total revenue, so the 'below 50%' point he cites is also right; Google Cloud doubled to $30.7bn.
rows.Notes: Same figures as Jason (1:01:24).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: There was literally a hoax, and those fake polls were included in those averages.
rows.Claim: Polling firms admitted publishing fake midterm polls, and those polls had been included in poll tracking.
rows.Evidence: In Oct 2026 Wedgewood Polls admitted almost all of its surveys (Michigan, Maine, Kansas, Mississippi, Nebraska) were fabricated, calling them an 'experimental project'; a second group's bogus polls in California, Nevada and Wisconsin surfaced in August. Aggregators had highlighted Wedgewood polls and the New York Times had listed 15 of them on its race tracking pages before removing them.
rows.Notes: His wider claims (a Patrick Ruffini study finding three-quarters of polls erred toward Democrats) were not verified and are not rated.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: You had Anne Seltzer, who was supposedly the gold standard, say that Trump was going to lose Iowa by like 10 or something like that, and it turned out to be total nonsense.
rows.Claim: Ann Selzer's final 2024 Iowa poll had Trump losing the state, and it was badly wrong.
rows.Evidence: Selzer's final Des Moines Register poll (Nov 2024) had Harris ahead 47-44, a 3-point lead, not 10. Trump won Iowa by about 13 points, a 16-point miss, and Selzer ended her election polling afterwards.
rows.Notes: The margin is overstated (Harris +3, not about 10), but the point, a badly wrong poll, stands (Methodology rule 3).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: Median household income is almost $90,000. It's at an all-time high. Poverty is at an all-time low.
rows.Claim: US median household income is near $90,000, a record high, and poverty is at a record low.
rows.Evidence: The Census Bureau's Sep 2026 report shows 2025 real median household income of $87,460, the highest on record (since 1967), and an official poverty rate of 10.2%, down 0.5 points and reported as the lowest on record.
rows.Notes: He then says the poverty rate is 'like 12%'; it is 10.2% (the Supplemental Poverty Measure is 13.1%). The record-low point stands.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: That was the first time Republicans took control of the House for the first time in 40 years.
rows.Claim: The 1994 midterms gave Republicans control of the House for the first time in 40 years.
rows.Evidence: In Nov 1994 Republicans led by Newt Gingrich, campaigning on the Contract with America, gained 54 House seats and took the majority for the first time since the 1952 election (40 years of Democratic control from 1955).
rows.Notes: Used to argue that a midterm loss for the party holding the White House is normal.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: I think it's still set up to have the Republicans keep the Senate and the Democrats to have a narrow majority.
rows.Claim: Republicans will keep the Senate and Democrats will win a narrow House majority in the 2026 midterms.
rows.Evidence: Repeats his 2 Oct prediction (AIA-20261002-16). At recording, prediction markets favoured Democrats in both chambers (Jason cites about 68% for the Senate and 92% for the House on Polymarket).
rows.Notes: Rule (auto): Accurate if Republicans hold a Senate majority (50+ seats with the VP tiebreak) AND Democrats win the House with 230 seats or fewer after the 3 Nov 2026 election; same thresholds as the signed-off rule for AIA-20261002-16. Partial (one chamber right) is Misleading, explained in Notes; False if both are wrong.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: So when you put all that together, I think it's a very easy sweep for the Democrats.
rows.Claim: Democrats will win both the House and the Senate in the 2026 midterms.
rows.Evidence: Repeats his 2 Oct prediction (AIA-20261002-17). He cites Polymarket at 68% for a Democratic Senate and 92% for a Democratic House.
rows.Notes: Rule (auto): Accurate if Democrats control both the House and the Senate after the 3 Nov 2026 election (Senate control counted with the VP tiebreak); False if they lose either chamber. Same rule as AIA-20261002-17.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: I think we're going to go right back to Trump being impeached, and then both houses are going to do that.
rows.Claim: After the midterms, Trump will be impeached again, with both chambers acting against him.
rows.Evidence: Trump has been impeached twice (2019, 2021) and acquitted by the Senate both times.
rows.Notes: Rule (auto): Accurate if the House impeaches Trump AND the Senate votes to convict on at least one article before 3 Jan 2029 (end of the 120th Congress); Misleading (partial) if the House impeaches but the Senate does not convict; False if the House does not impeach him by 3 Jan 2029. 'Both houses are going to do that' is read as House impeachment plus Senate conviction.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: And then I think that means they put JD Vance and Marco Rubio to bed, and they're going to need a new champion that is more populist
rows.Claim: Republicans will pass over JD Vance and Marco Rubio for a new, more populist 2028 nominee.
rows.Evidence: He says this is his analysis, not his personal wish. Both are among the leading names for the 2028 Republican nomination.
rows.Notes: Rule (auto): Accurate if the 2028 Republican presidential nominee (chosen at the 2028 Republican National Convention) is neither JD Vance nor Marco Rubio; False if either is the nominee. The 'more populist' part is not scored. Void if no nomination is made by 31 Aug 2028.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Anthropic S-1 Shocker, Greatest Business Ever? Google's $500B Wipeout, Midterm Predictions
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: 200 customers in 2024 end of year, 1,500 end of 2025, and at the end of September, 11,900 customers spending $100K or more.
rows.Claim: Anthropic's customers spending $100k+ a year went from about 200 at end-2024 to 1,500 at end-2025 and 11,900 at the end of Sep 2026.
rows.Evidence: The S-1 reports more than 11,900 customers above $100k of trailing-twelve-month revenue as of 30 Sep 2026. Analysis of the filing puts the end-2025 count at about 1,500 and says the count roughly doubled in Q3. The end-2024 figure of 200 was not found in the filing excerpts reviewed.
rows.Notes: Latest figure verified; earlier counts only approximately. His follow-on estimate that Anthropic is about 1% penetrated is his own analysis and not rated.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Obviously, the Democrats sweeped both chambers of Congress, and they won at least 29 governor races.
rows.Claim: Democrats won both the House and the Senate in the 2026 midterms, and at least 29 governor races.
rows.Evidence: Democrats won majorities in both chambers on 3 Nov 2026. Of the 36 governor races, Democrats had won 23 and Republicans 12 at recording, with Kansas uncalled; Democrats flipped Alaska, Georgia, Iowa, Nevada, Ohio and Texas and lost none.
rows.Notes: The 29 figure matches the total number of Democratic governors from 2027 (about 29-30 of 50), not governor races won this year (23 of 36). The sweep, which is the point, stands (Methodology rule 3).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Dems will wind up with 54, 55, or 56 seats, depending on how Alaska and Mississippi wind up. They have a lot of votes still coming in, in the House. Dems will have at least 250 seats, maybe even 260
rows.Claim: Democrats will end up with 54-56 Senate seats depending on Alaska and Mississippi, and at least 250 House seats.
rows.Evidence: At recording Democrats had 54 Senate seats to 44, with Alaska (Peltola leading by about 640 votes) and Mississippi (Colom leading by about 2,500) uncalled. In the House Democrats had 253 called seats with 20 uncalled, and were winning or leading in about 259; they held 215 before the election.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Kansas, Iowa, South Carolina, for the first time in decades, Trump won all of those states by double digits just two years ago.
rows.Claim: Democrats won statewide races in Texas, Kansas, Iowa and South Carolina, states Trump carried by double digits in 2024.
rows.Evidence: Democrats won Senate seats in Texas (Talarico), Kansas (Hamilton), Iowa (Turek) and South Carolina (Andrews), and the governorships of Texas (Hinojosa) and Iowa (Sand). Trump carried Kansas by about 16 points, Iowa by about 13 and South Carolina by about 18 in 2024.
rows.Notes: 2024 margins are from the certified 2024 results; the 2026 Kansas governor race was still uncalled at recording.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Compared to 2024, the GOP lost ground in every voter group, even white men.
rows.Claim: Republicans lost ground with every voter group compared with 2024, including white men.
rows.Evidence: Exit-poll comparisons show large shifts to Democrats in most groups, including white men (about 17 points) and men overall (R+14 to D+2). But some groups moved the other way: the Democratic lead among Jewish voters fell from 50 to 37 points and among Latinos 65+ from 16 to 10, and white evangelicals barely moved.
rows.Notes: The broad swing is real; 'every voter group' is not.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: It was, I believe, the biggest midterm loss since the Watergate midterm loss.
rows.Claim: Republicans' 2026 midterm loss was the biggest since the 1974 Watergate midterms.
rows.Evidence: Democrats' net House gain (about 44 seats at recording) is smaller than Republicans' gains in 2010 (63) and 1994 (54), though larger than 2018 (41) and below 1974 (49). In the Senate Democrats had flipped 7 seats, reaching 9 only if they win both Alaska and Mississippi; Republicans gained 8 in 1994.
rows.Notes: It was a historic blowout, which is his point, but by House seats at least two post-Watergate midterms were bigger. Hedged ('I believe'). Revisit if final Senate count reaches 56.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: Price of gas. It was around $3 before the war went over $4 and higher. Price of diesel, even higher.
rows.Claim: US gasoline was about $3 a gallon before the Iran war and rose above $4; diesel rose even more.
rows.Evidence: EIA's weekly regular gasoline price was $2.937 in the week of 23 Feb 2026, just before the war began on 28 Feb, and $4.153 on 2 Nov, with a 2026 peak around $4.50 in May. Diesel went from $3.809 to $6.292 over the same period.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: you saw the inflation rate at the beginning of the year, back in January before the war, it was down to 2.4 percent. We finally had that problem licked just about. Remember, it was 9 percent under Biden.
rows.Claim: CPI inflation was 2.4% in January 2026, down from 9% under Biden, and has since risen to 3.7%.
rows.Evidence: BLS: CPI rose 2.4% in the 12 months to January 2026 and 3.7% in the 12 months to September 2026 (the latest release); he gives the 3.7% figure at 6:07. The 9% refers to the June 2022 peak of 9.1%.
rows.Notes: 9% was a single-month peak, not the Biden-era average.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: the prediction markets back in January were showing a 70 percent chance of Republicans holding the Senate. And then the House was perceived to be a toss up.
rows.Claim: In January 2026 prediction markets gave Republicans about a 70% chance of holding the Senate, and the House was a toss-up.
rows.Evidence: Kalshi's own write-up says traders gave Republicans 'about a two-in-three chance' of keeping the Senate in January 2026, close to his 70%.
rows.Notes: Rated on the Senate figure, which carries his argument. No January House price was found; by May Kalshi had Democrats at 76%, so 'toss-up' is doubtful and unverified.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: you end up not having any rate cuts. You end up getting a rate hike. That brought the cost of mortgages to roughly 7.5 percent.
rows.Claim: There were no Fed rate cuts in 2026, there was a hike, and mortgage rates rose to about 7.5%.
rows.Evidence: The Fed held at 3.50-3.75% from January and raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 Sep 2026, its first hike in over three years; it held on 28 Oct. Freddie Mac's 30-year average peaked at 7.40% (8 and 15 Oct) and was 7.18% on 5 Nov.
rows.Notes: Slightly overstated: the peak was 7.40%, not 7.5%.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: You've got unemployment ticked down to almost record low, 4.1%.
rows.Claim: Unemployment fell to 4.1%, almost a record low.
rows.Evidence: BLS's October 2026 report puts unemployment at 4.1%, which it describes as 'changed little'; it has been between 4.1% and 4.3% since March. The record low is 2.5% (1953), and the rate was 3.4% as recently as 2023, so 4.1% is not near a record. Payrolls rose 165,000 and Aug-Sep were revised up 84,000, as he says.
rows.Notes: The 4.1% and the upward revisions are right; 'almost record low' gives a wrong picture of the labor market.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: In the first half of the year, it was around 2.1% to 2.5%. And then third quarter, the tracking by GDP now is 3.7%.
rows.Claim: US GDP grew about 2.1-2.5% in H1 2026, and Q3 is tracking 3.7%.
rows.Evidence: BEA: Q1 2026 grew 2.1% and Q2 2.2% (annualized). BEA's advance estimate for Q3, published 29 Oct, was 3.4%. The 3.7% he cites was the Atlanta Fed GDPNow estimate for Q4 on 2 Nov (cut to 3.4% on 4 Nov).
rows.Notes: He mixes up quarters (Q3 is already published at 3.4%), but the point, solid growth, stands (Methodology rule 3).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: in the first year of the Trump administration, we made enormous progress in delivering real post-tax household income. It rose by like 3.1%.
rows.Claim: Real post-tax household income rose about 3.1% in 2025, Trump's first year back.
rows.Evidence: The Census Bureau's Sep 2026 report shows real post-tax median household income of $76,060 in 2025, up 3.1% from $73,760 in 2024. Pre-tax real median household income rose 2.6% to a record $87,460.
rows.Notes: Other measures are lower: BEA real disposable personal income rose 1.6% in 2025 (1.1% per capita).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: It was negative during the Biden years and it was positive during Trump 45
rows.Claim: Real household income fell during Biden's presidency and rose during Trump's first term.
rows.Evidence: Census real median household income fell 0.6% in 2021 (not statistically significant) and 2.3% in 2022, then rose 4.0% in 2023 and about 1.3% in 2024, leaving it higher in 2024 than in 2020. BEA real disposable income per capita fell 6.1% in 2022 but rose in 2023 and 2024.
rows.Notes: True for 2021-22, not for the Biden term as a whole. The Trump 45 part was not separately checked.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: the average household is paying 200 bucks a month more in gas costs.
rows.Claim: Since the Iran war began, the average US household is paying about $200 a month more for gas.
rows.Evidence: Brown University's Sep 2026 estimate is that each household paid over $750 more for gasoline and diesel from 28 Feb to 7 Sep, about $120 a month; Moody's Mark Zandi put the total energy cost at about $860 per household. A roughly $1.10-1.20 rise per gallon on typical household use gives about $100 a month.
rows.Notes: Available estimates are about $100-130 a month, so $200 overstates the hit by more than half.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: Young males flipped their vote by 36 points in this midterm relative to the 2024 election.
rows.Claim: Young men swung 36 points toward Democrats compared with 2024.
rows.Evidence: Estimates of the swing among young men vary widely: Newsweek's exit-poll comparison has men under 30 at D+35 in 2026; CIRCLE has young men 58-38 Democratic; AP VoteCast has 39% of men under 30 voting Republican versus more than half for Trump in 2024. Published swing figures range from about 22 to 45 points.
rows.Notes: A big swing is clear; the 36-point figure depends on the poll and the 2024 baseline used.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: Crucial, 34 percent, a major factor, 40 percent.
rows.Claim: In exit polls, 34% of voters called the Iran war crucial to their vote and 40% a major factor.
rows.Evidence: Election-day exit polling showed 34% calling the Iran war crucial, 40% a major factor and 19% a minor factor. The war began with US strikes on 28 Feb 2026, the date he gives.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: On the day of the election, the price of Brent crude dropped 10%.
rows.Claim: Brent crude fell about 10% around election day as markets priced in an earlier end to the war.
rows.Evidence: Brent (Jan 2027 contract) fell 1.1% on 3 Nov, election day, then 8.7-9.7% on 4 Nov to about $93.5-94.6; from 30 Oct ($113.43) to 4 Nov it fell 17.6%. The 2026 peak was about $118 (late March) to $126 intraday (30 Apr), consistent with his 'as high as 117'.
rows.Notes: The roughly 10% drop came the day after the election, not on it; the point stands.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: it'll go from 110 to 70
rows.Claim: If the Iran war ends, Brent crude will fall from about $110 to about $70.
rows.Evidence: Brent was about $94-105 in the week of recording; it traded near $70-74 in June-July 2026. He makes the drop conditional on the war ending.
rows.Notes: Rule (auto): Void if no end to US-Iran hostilities (a ceasefire or peace agreement announced by the US government) by 31 Dec 2027. If it ends: Accurate if the Brent front-month contract settles at or below $75 on any day within 90 days of the announcement; Misleading (partial) if the lowest settlement in that window is $75-85; False if it stays above $85. Data: ICE Brent settlement as reported by EIA (RBRTE) or Reuters.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Trump started the term at 5% plus net approval rating. He ended it at negative 28
rows.Claim: Trump's net approval went from about +5 at the start of his term to -28 now, a swing of over 30 points.
rows.Evidence: The Silver Bulletin average he cites had Trump at 38.3% approve and about 59% disapprove on 6 Nov 2026, a net of about -21 (-22.8 on 29 Oct). Polling averages had him around +5 in late January 2025. Only Civiqs (registered voters) shows about -27.
rows.Notes: The decline is real and large (about 26 points), but the end figure and 'over 30% swing', which are his point, are overstated on the source he names.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Remember, he had to go to the Supreme Court. He lost there.
rows.Claim: Trump lost at the Supreme Court over his emergency (IEEPA) tariffs.
rows.Evidence: In Learning Resources v. Trump, decided 20 Feb 2026, the Supreme Court held that IEEPA does not authorize the tariffs; Chief Justice Roberts wrote the majority opinion.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: Look what happened of the 15 Republican seats that were redrawn so that they could capture all of them. Democrats won 11 of them. Republicans only won one.
rows.Claim: Of 15 House seats Republicans redrew to win, Democrats won 11 and Republicans only one.
rows.Evidence: Reporting on the 2025-26 mid-decade redistricting counts 15 GOP-targeted seats, of which Democrats won 11. Roll Call shows Republicans winning two of the targeted seats (TX-32 and TN-9), with others uncalled or in runoffs.
rows.Notes: 'Only one' looks to be two; the point, that the redraw backfired, stands.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: And on June 5th of 2025, Elon left and it was the end of Doge.
rows.Claim: Elon Musk left DOGE on 5 June 2025, effectively ending it.
rows.Evidence: Musk announced his exit on 28 May 2025 and was offboarded around 30 May, when his special-employee term ran out. 5 June 2025 was the day of his public feud with Trump.
rows.Notes: The date is about a week off (he conflates the exit with the feud); the point, that the DOGE push ended in mid-2025, stands. His 'China has just won' tweet on 5 June could not be checked.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: And we're still running a $7 trillion a year government budget with a $2 trillion a year deficit.
rows.Claim: The federal government spends about $7tn a year and runs a deficit of about $2tn.
rows.Evidence: CBO: FY2026 outlays were $7.396tn and the deficit $1.993tn; FY2025 outlays were $7.010tn with a $1.775tn deficit.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: The US is fourth-last. We are worse than Afghanistan. And we're just slightly better than Malawi and Bangladesh. We're fourth on the list of countries, at 36% of Americans believing that.
rows.Claim: In Gallup's survey, 93% of Chinese but only 36% of Americans think AI will mostly help, putting the US fourth-last, below Afghanistan.
rows.Evidence: Gallup's 37-country survey shows China at 93% and the US at 36% saying AI will mostly help people in their country. The lowest are Bangladesh (34%), Egypt and Malawi (35%), then the US; Afghanistan is 37%.
rows.Notes: Gallup's text calls the US third-lowest, apparently counting tied countries together; by the table it is fourth-last.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: And the reason is we doubled government spending.
rows.Claim: During COVID the US doubled federal government spending.
rows.Evidence: Federal outlays were $4.447tn in FY2019, $6.552tn in FY2020 (+47%) and $6.817tn in FY2021 (+53% on FY2019). Spending rose by about half, not double, and fell back to $6.27tn in FY2022.
rows.Notes: The size of the increase carries his argument that spending drove inflation; 'doubled' overstates it.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: But this was the worst single day in the history of the stock market by total dollars
rows.Claim: This week's AI sell-off wiped close to $4tn off stocks, the worst single day ever in dollar terms.
rows.Evidence: On Thu 5 Nov 2026 the S&P 500 fell 4.4%, losing about $2.9tn, which Dow Jones Market Data calls the largest one-day dollar loss on record (previous record about $2.69tn on 16 Mar 2020). AMD and Micron fell about 15%, Tesla up to 10% and Nvidia almost 9%.
rows.Notes: His 'close to $4 trillion' (also in the episode title) is high: estimates run $2.9-3.2tn. The record, which is his point, stands.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: the Wall Street Journal reported today that the hair cut could be baked in now.
rows.Claim: The WSJ reported that Anthropic's IPO valuation may be cut to about $1tn from the $1.5-2tn expected.
rows.Evidence: The WSJ reported on Thu 5 Nov 2026 that Anthropic's IPO valuation would likely need to come down from the roughly $1.5tn expected, with one investor saying it could be closer to $1tn.
rows.Notes: The report was a day before recording, not 'today'. The Polymarket odds he cites (95% to 71%) were found as about 95% to 77% for Anthropic; odds are context only. Anthropic row: extra scrutiny per Methodology s.9; Jason notes Polymarket is a show partner.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: SpaceX and Anthropic's compute deal has a mutual 90 day out.
rows.Claim: Anthropic's compute deal with SpaceX can be cancelled by either side on 90 days' notice.
rows.Evidence: Anthropic's amended S-1, as quoted in analysis of the filing, says each SpaceX agreement 'may be cancelled by either party upon 90 days' advance written notice', after initial non-cancellable periods that end in January 2027 and March 2027. Committed spend is up to $120.5bn through 2029.
rows.Notes: The mutual out applies only after the lock-up periods. Anthropic row: extra scrutiny per Methodology s.9.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: Chamath Palihapitiya
rows.Quote: Google just took over a Crusoe data center.
rows.Claim: Google has taken over a data center project that Crusoe was developing.
rows.Evidence: On 6 Nov 2026 Crusoe announced that Google had acquired its southeast Wyoming data center site, developed with Tallgrass (Bloomberg: 'Google Takes Over Wyoming Data Center That Crusoe Had Pitched').
rows.Notes: It is a pre-construction site (permits and power planning done), not an operating data center.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: She does not say that existing projects are protected. She simply says that there'll be no new permits issued until they pass legislation dealing with the issues she's talking about.
rows.Claim: Texas governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has promised no new data center permits until legislation passes, and has not said existing projects are protected.
rows.Evidence: In a 22 Oct video Hinojosa pledged 'a moratorium, a ban, on all data center approvals' until the Legislature passes protections; her campaign tied this to the session starting in January. The Texas Tribune notes she did not address already-approved or under-construction projects. SemiAnalysis warns that projects needing later approvals could be stalled.
rows.Notes: He adds that he is not criticizing her and does not know what she will do.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: You've got our biggest data center states where there's basically been a regime change. All those governors are basically indicating that they favor moratorium until XYZ happens.
rows.Claim: The biggest data-center states have new governors who all favor moratoriums on data centers.
rows.Evidence: Texas, Georgia and Ohio switched to Democratic governors who back a moratorium or conditional halt (Hinojosa, Bottoms, Acton). But Virginia's Gov. Spanberger, elected in 2025, rejected a statewide pause in Aug 2026 ('That is a local choice'), and Arizona did not change hands (Hobbs re-elected).
rows.Notes: True for several of the largest states, not for 'all'; Virginia, the largest, is the main exception.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: When you're talking about infrastructure of this magnitude, these gigawatt power data centers, they cost around $50 billion.
rows.Claim: A 1-gigawatt AI data center costs about $50bn.
rows.Evidence: Nvidia's Jensen Huang has put the cost of a 1-GW AI facility at $50-60bn including chips; SpaceX's proposed 6-GW Cochise County campus is reported at up to $50bn.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: But I think by 2028, I would expect that the pipeline will either be closed or significantly reduced and that will have a big economic impact.
rows.Claim: Fully permitted data centers will still be built in 2027, but by 2028 the US data center pipeline will be closed or significantly reduced.
rows.Evidence: US private data center construction hit a record of about $96.5bn (annual rate) in September 2026, per Census data as reported; SemiAnalysis says 2027 capacity is largely locked in.
rows.Notes: Rule (auto): Uses the Census Bureau Construction Spending (C30) series for private 'data center' construction (under Office). Accurate if the 2028 annual total is at least 15% below the 2027 annual total; Misleading (partial) if it is 0-15% below; False if 2028 is equal to or higher than 2027. Scored on the first annual figures published after year-end 2028 (by 1 Jul 2029). The blame part ('Democrats will try to blame the president') is not scored.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: Okay, so it's 100% that Democrats are going to make a major push for AI legislation in the next Congress.
rows.Claim: Democrats will make a major push for federal AI legislation, such as a federal AI department reviewing frontier models, in the next Congress.
rows.Evidence: Democrats take control of both chambers on 3 Jan 2027. No comprehensive federal AI law existed at recording.
rows.Notes: Rule (auto): Accurate if, during the 120th Congress (by 3 Jan 2029), a bill that creates a federal AI agency or office, or requires federal licensing or pre-release review of frontier AI models, is reported out of committee or passes either chamber; False if no such bill gets that far. 'Major push' is pinned to committee approval. His description of what it will contain ('surveillance and censorship state') is not scored.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: I think it's going to be very hard with this Congress and the sitting president to come to a resolution on a clean budget. And as a result, I think things are going to continue as is.
rows.Claim: With a Democratic Congress and Trump, there will be no clean budget in 2027, and the spending and deficit picture will stay as it is.
rows.Evidence: FY2026 deficit was $1.993tn (CBO).
rows.Notes: Rule (auto): Accurate if the 12 regular FY2028 appropriations bills are not all enacted by 1 Oct 2027 (government runs on a continuing resolution or shuts down) AND CBO reports an FY2027 deficit of $1.8tn or more; Misleading (partial) if only one holds; False if neither.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Sacks
rows.Quote: I do think that President Trump deserves enormous credit for completely sealing the border and solving that immigration issue.
rows.Claim: Trump has sealed the southern border.
rows.Evidence: Southwest border apprehensions in FY2026 were 98,708 (about 270 a day), a historic low and about 95% below the Biden-era peak of over 1.8m a year, per a DHS/CBP announcement as reported.
rows.Notes: 'Completely sealing' is hyperbole (tens of thousands are still apprehended a year); rated on the literal core, record-low crossings (Methodology rule 2). Source is secondary; the DHS page did not load.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: Ninety-nine percent of their prediction markets turned out to have it perfectly.
rows.Claim: About 99% of Polymarket's election markets called the midterm results correctly.
rows.Evidence: Polymarket reported that the favorite won in 419 of 427 settled midterm markets (98.4%), with 78 unsettled; Kalshi claimed a similar rate. Misses included the South Carolina Senate race and Hinojosa's win in Texas.
rows.Notes: Polymarket is a partner of the show (he says so at 53:13).

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: Jason Calacanis
rows.Quote: And in fact, it's only 10, 15 million people who are impacted by under $15 an hour.
rows.Claim: Only 10-15 million US workers earn under $15 an hour.
rows.Evidence: The most recent solid estimate found (EPI, CPS data Dec 2021-Nov 2022) is about 21 million workers under $15; Oxfam (2022) put it at 52 million. No 2025-26 national count was found; wage growth since 2022 has likely lowered the number.
rows.Notes: Searched for BLS/EPI counts for 2025-26; none found.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: And they disproved it in a 175-page paper
rows.Claim: OpenAI has disproved the Exponential Time Hypothesis, posed in 1999, in a long paper produced in under 10 days.
rows.Evidence: OpenAI posted 'The Exponential Time Hypothesis is False' (preprint plus Lean proof) on 26 Oct 2026; Anthropic posted a separate refutation. ETH was proposed by Impagliazzo and Paturi in 1999. The model produced the proof on 16 Oct and it was formalised in Lean on 17 Oct. Impagliazzo, Paturi and Ryan Williams are reviewing it; no flaw had been found by early November.
rows.Notes: The paper is reported as 67 pages, not 175. Not yet independently verified, as he notes. Rated on the claim that OpenAI produced a proof refuting ETH.

rows.EpisodeTitle: Midterm Blood Bath, $4T AI Sell Off, Data Center Freeze, What's Next for Trump
rows.Speaker: David Friedberg
rows.Quote: And what that means is that P could still equal NP, which means that theoretically every problem in the universe can be solved with a computer.
rows.Claim: Disproving ETH keeps open the possibility that P equals NP, i.e. that every problem could be solved by computer.
rows.Evidence: ETH was always an unproven conjecture, stronger than P!=NP; it was never 'demonstrated', as he says earlier. Refuting it leaves P vs NP exactly as open as before: the claimed bound (about 2^(n/sqrt(log n))) is still superpolynomial. Ryan Williams says it breaks no existing cryptosystem, and Anthropic says its method only beats brute force at more than 10^10,000 variables.
rows.Notes: P=NP was always possible; presenting it as a consequence of this result overstates what it means. P=NP would also not mean 'every problem in the universe' is computable.
